newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Rebels threaten to pull out of talks with Manila.
newsitem.headline: Rebels threaten to pull out of talks with Manila.

text.p: Moslem rebels on Monday threatened to pull out of ceasefire talks with Manila and launch a major offensive if the Philippine military attacked their main camp on southern Mindanao island.
Al Haj Murad, military vice chairman of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF), issued the warning after fresh fighting erupted near a rebel camp which soldiers captured two weeks ago.
Armed forces chief General Arnulfo Acedera told reporters "about 150 rebels," 15 soldiers and five civilians had died in fighting in Mindanao since mid-June.
Officials said the figure on rebel losses was based largely on reports from villagers fleeing battle zones. There was no confirmation from independent sources.

"All indications point to Camp Abubakar...as the next target of massive (military) aggression," Murad said. "Should this happen, we shall be left with no alternative but to abandon the peace negotiations and launch counter-offensives," he said in a statement.
About 6,000 guerrillas are estimated by the military to be entrenched in the sprawling MILF camp in Maguindanao province.
Murad said Manila would be responsible "if a full-blown war explodes in Mindanao."
The MILF postponed ceasefire talks last month after soldiers overran Camp Rajamuda, its second biggest base in Mindanao.

Five soldiers were wounded when the rebels shelled the government-occupied camp in the latest fighting on Monday. The MILF is fighting for an Islamic state and was not a part of the peace deal Manila signed last year with the mainstream Moro National Liberation Front (MNLF).
